title: 轮到我了
subtitle: 排队、轮流和等一等
character: wearing a yellow t-shirt, blue shorts and white sneakers, short black hair
style: children's picture book illustration, wax crayon resist: thick white and bright crayon lines showing through a soft watercolor wash painted over them, textured paper, cheerful colors

pages.zh:
下午，妈妈带我去公园。
公园里有一个高高的滑梯，
黄黄的，弯弯的。
我一看见就想冲过去。
pages.scene: A sunny park with a tall yellow curly slide. The little boy runs toward it with his arms up, happy and excited.

pages.zh:
可是滑梯前面，
已经站着三个小朋友。
他们一个跟着一个，
排成一条小队伍。
pages.scene: Three other children of different ages stand in a neat line at the bottom of the slide ladder, and the little boy stops right behind them, looking at the line.

pages.zh:
我好想马上就滑。
脚在原地跳来跳去，
手也痒痒的。
妈妈说：
「大家轮流，一个一个来。」
pages.scene: The little boy stands at the end of the line bouncing on his toes, looking up at the slide, his hands fidgeting, other children ahead of him on the ladder.

pages.zh:
「轮流」是什么意思呢？
就是每个人都玩一会儿，
玩完就换下一个。
这样大家都能玩到，
谁也不会一直等下去。
pages.scene: A simple clear picture: four children's coloured footprints drawn in a row on the ground leading to a slide, with a number 1, 2, 3, 4 marked beside each pair of footprints.

pages.zh:
等待的时候，
我数了数前面还有几个人。
三个，两个，一个……
数着数着，
好像没有那么难等了。
pages.scene: The little boy stands in the line counting on his fingers, looking at the two children still in front of him, a calm patient face.

pages.zh:
轮到我了！
我抓住扶手，一级一级爬上去，
坐好，
然后——嗖！
滑下来的风吹到我的脸上。
pages.scene: The little boy slides down the yellow slide with both arms up, laughing, his hair blown back by the wind.

pages.zh:
滑完了，我没有再爬上去，
而是从旁边跑回队伍后面，
重新排好。
后面的小朋友也想滑呢。
pages.scene: The little boy walks back around the side of the slide to the end of the line, while another child climbs the ladder behind him.

pages.zh:
秋千也要轮流。
公园里只有两个秋千，
想荡的人却有好几个。
所以大家说好：
数到二十就换人。
pages.scene: Two empty swings hanging side by side in a park, with a small chalk number 20 drawn on the ground in front of them.

pages.zh:
我坐上秋千，
荡呀荡，
心里数：一、二、三……
数到二十的时候，
我停下来，跳下秋千。
pages.scene: The little boy swings on a park swing with his legs stretched out, his mouth moving as he counts, a happy face.

pages.zh:
我把秋千让给后面的小妹妹。
她说了一声「谢谢」。
她笑起来的时候，
我心里也变得暖暖的。
pages.scene: The little boy holds the swing steady with one hand while a smaller girl with pigtails climbs onto it, both smiling at each other.

pages.zh:
沙坑里只有一把小铲子。
两个人都想用，
怎么办呢？
我们把沙漏放在旁边，
沙子漏完就换人。
pages.scene: A sandpit with one yellow spade lying in the sand and a small hourglass standing beside it, sunlight on the sand, no people.

pages.zh:
轮到别人的时候，
我就在旁边堆我的小山。
手上没有铲子，
可是用手也能堆。
等一等，也能玩得很开心。
pages.scene: The little boy kneels in the sandpit piling up a small sand hill with his bare hands, another child digging with the spade nearby, both busy and content.

pages.zh:
有个小哥哥直接插到了队伍前面。
我有点生气，
可是我没有推他。
我说：
「请排到后面，我们在轮流。」
pages.scene: The little boy stands in the line and speaks up calmly to a bigger boy who has stepped in front of him, pointing with his open hand toward the end of the line, other children waiting behind.

pages.zh:
要是他还是不听，
我就去找大人帮忙。
公园里有妈妈，
幼儿园里有老师，
大人会帮我们把事情说清楚。
pages.scene: A grown adult woman with short black hair in a red sweater sits on a park bench looking toward the playground, ready to help, warm afternoon light.

pages.zh:
图书角也是一样。
我想看的那本恐龙书，
正被别的小朋友捧在手里。
那我就先看另一本，
等他看完再换。
pages.scene: A cosy reading corner with a low shelf of picture books, one dinosaur book missing from the shelf and a gap where it was, a cushion on the floor, no people.

pages.zh:
等待的时候，
心里会痒痒的，有点着急。
这时候可以深呼吸，
可以数数，
也可以先做点别的事。
pages.scene: The little boy sits cross-legged on a cushion in the reading corner with his eyes closed, taking a slow deep breath, a picture book open on his lap.

pages.zh:
轮到我的时候，
我拿到了那本恐龙书。
因为等过，
所以拿到的时候，
特别开心。
pages.scene: The little boy sits on a cushion holding the dinosaur picture book open with both hands, smiling widely at the pages.

pages.zh:
回家的路上，妈妈说：
「你今天很会等。」
我想了想，
等一等，其实没有那么难。
而且大家都玩到了。
pages.scene: The little boy walks home along a tree-lined path holding the hand of his mother, a grown adult woman with short black hair in a red sweater, in the late afternoon sun, both smiling, the park behind them.
